records.title: ISO 1996-2:2017 — Determination of environmental sound pressure levels
records.released_version: Edition 3, July 2017; official record says current/confirmed in 2026, while its lifecycle contains a to-be-revised event.
records.locator: ISO official product abstract, status and lifecycle.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and reviewed the scope, uncertainty statement, and lifecycle preview.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Primarily outdoor environmental sound determination; measurement effort is selected by the user and uncertainty is to be determined and reported; no allowable maximum uncertainty is set by this standard.
records.applicability: Supports framing a separate courtyard outcome and reporting uncertainty; does not identify this building's path or set a local resident/legal threshold.

records.title: ISO 16283-1:2014 — Airborne sound insulation between rooms
records.released_version: Edition 1, February 2014, Amendment 1:2017; official record says reviewed/confirmed in 2025.
records.locator: ISO official product abstract, amendment and lifecycle.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and reviewed its scope, range, amendment, and status.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Field procedures determine airborne sound insulation between two rooms; intended room volume 10-250 m3 and frequency range 50 Hz-5 kHz; measured insulation is frequency-dependent.
records.applicability: Possible later room-to-room airborne follow-up only; does not measure structural vibration or ambient courtyard sound, and its frequency floor limits very-low-bass inference.

records.title: ISO 16283-3:2016 — Façade sound insulation
records.released_version: Edition 1, February 2016; official status says published and to be revised, with ISO/CD 16283-3 under development.
records.locator: ISO official product abstract and lifecycle.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and reviewed the façade scope, frequency/volume range, and lifecycle.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Airborne façade-element and whole-façade methods; intended room volume 10-250 m3 and 50 Hz-5 kHz; current edition marked for revision.
records.applicability: Later façade airborne investigation with suitable access/equipment only; not a courtyard ambient-noise or structure-borne test and not evidence of site performance.

records.title: ISO 10052:2021 — Survey method for airborne/impact insulation and service-equipment sound
records.released_version: Edition 2, 2021, ISO Online Browsing Platform English record.
records.locator: OBP foreword, introduction, scope, survey procedure, and precision notes.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO OBP text and reviewed the introduction and scope.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Simplified survey uses a handheld sound-level instrument and manual microphone sweep; airborne/impact/façade insulation results are octave-band dependent; applicable rooms are dwellings/comparable rooms up to 150 m3; a priori uncertainty is greater than corresponding engineering methods. Annex operating cycles apply only when consistent with national requirements.
records.applicability: Supports bounded screening only; it does not turn a basic meter, phone, or improvised music test into a formal insulation assessment.

records.title: ISO 3382-2:2008 — Reverberation time in ordinary rooms
records.released_version: Edition 1, June 2008; Corrigendum 1:2009; official record says confirmed in 2022.
records.locator: ISO official product abstract and lifecycle.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and reviewed its method scope and lifecycle.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Specifies procedures, apparatus, positions, data evaluation, and reporting for room reverberation-time measurement.
records.applicability: Internal room-decay result only; does not establish a reduction in courtyard disturbance.

records.title: ISO 23591:2021 — Acoustic quality criteria for music rehearsal rooms and spaces
records.released_version: Edition 1, September 2021, Amendment 1:2025 (Asian/Korean traditional music); official page shows systematic review activity.
records.locator: ISO official product abstract, amendment, and lifecycle.
records.observed_operation: Opened the ISO official product page and reviewed criteria scope, amendment, and status.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Differentiates amplified, quiet acoustic, and loud acoustic rehearsal uses and includes room height/volume/area criteria; explicitly excludes sound-insulation criteria.
records.applicability: Can frame room suitability after music type and dimensions are known; cannot set a neighbor-noise or façade target.

records.title: Pedersen, Møller & Persson Waye (2007), Indoor Measurements of Noise at Low Frequencies — Problems and Solutions
records.released_version: Journal of Low Frequency Noise, Vibration and Active Control, 26(4), 249-270, 2007; DOI 10.1260/026309207783571389.
records.observed_operation: Opened the primary journal article page and reviewed the abstract and publication details; full text was not needed for the claim checked.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Abstract reports up to 20-30 dB low-frequency spatial variation based on simulations and measurement distributions in three rooms, and discusses methods that risk missing high-level locations.
records.applicability: Supports several marked room positions/repeatability; reported magnitude and proposed room method are not predictions for this building.

records.title: Løvholt et al. (2017), Simulating low frequency sound transmission through walls and windows by a two-way coupled fluid-structure interaction model
records.released_version: Journal of Sound and Vibration, 396, 203-216, published 26 May 2017; DOI 10.1016/j.jsv.2017.02.026.
records.locator: Elsevier/ScienceDirect publisher abstract; direct-open tool error, abstract surfaced in publisher-hosted search result.
records.observed_operation: Searched the exact title/DOI and read the publisher-hosted abstract; a separate direct open returned an internal error. Full paper not read.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Abstract describes finite-element two-way fluid-structure simulations compared with laboratory wall/window tests from 10-100 Hz; structural connections matter, with different wall/window contributions by band; source context includes aircraft, supersonic flights, blasts and explosions.
records.applicability: Supports coexistence and interaction of air and structure routes and the need for path-sensitive measurements; laboratory assemblies/source spectra do not predict this building.

reviser_verification.locator: ScienceDirect publisher abstract surfaced by exact-title/DOI search; direct open returned an internal error.
reviser_verification.observed_operation: Attempted direct open of the exact publisher URL, which returned an internal error; searched the exact title and DOI and read the ScienceDirect-hosted publisher abstract.
reviser_verification.governing_condition_default_exception: The abstract describes two-way fluid–structure finite-element simulations compared with laboratory measurements for plain walls and walls with windows from 10–100 Hz. It reports that structural connections matter, windows control transmission from 15–30 Hz, and walls from 30–100 Hz; source context includes aircraft, supersonic flights, blasts and explosions.
reviser_verification.applicability: Supports interaction and frequency-dependent wall/window contributions in tested assemblies, not a unique-path diagnostic or prediction for this unknown rehearsal building.

records.title: Norén-Cosgriff et al. (2016), Countermeasures against noise and vibrations in lightweight wooden buildings caused by outdoor sources with strong low-frequency components
records.locator: SINTEF institutional publication abstract and bibliographic record.
records.observed_operation: Opened SINTEF's author-institution page and reviewed its abstract and publication metadata.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Research combined laboratory measurement, finite-element simulation, designed structural countermeasures, and full-scale tests in a Norwegian lightweight wooden building under F-16 aircraft noise; it measured indoor sound and floor vibration.
records.applicability: Supports measuring vibration alongside sound and illustrates a plausible mechanism; source/building and interventions differ, so numeric reductions are not transferable.

reviser_verification.locator: SINTEF institutional publication page, abstract and bibliographic record.
reviser_verification.observed_operation: Opened the exact SINTEF publication page and reviewed its abstract, methods summary and bibliographic details.
reviser_verification.governing_condition_default_exception: The record describes laboratory measurements, finite-element simulation, countermeasure design and full-scale field testing in a typical Norwegian wooden building under F-16 aircraft noise; it reports that transmitted low-frequency sound excited floor vibration in that study. Reported countermeasure results are specific to that source and building.
reviser_verification.applicability: Supports including synchronized vibration observation as a possible measurement; does not establish structure-borne transmission, a treatment effect or a site result here.

records.title: Vargas Vera, San Millán-Castillo & Swerdlow (2019), Sound insulation design methodology: case study on a music rehearsal room
records.released_version: Acoustics in Practice, vol. 7, no. 1, January 2019; 10-page EAA-hosted paper; no DOI identified in its record.
records.locator: Primary PDF abstract and methodology/conclusion sections.
records.observed_operation: Opened the EAA-hosted primary PDF and checked its case scope, repeated-source procedure, and stated verification boundary.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Residential-house basement case includes bass guitar, guitar, and drums; uses repeated 20-second musical fragments for source characterization, measures current enclosure, and models candidate solutions. Paper explicitly leaves verification of proposed solutions outside its scope.
records.applicability: Close source/use workflow analogue and a useful data-gathering lead, not proof of an installed solution or structural-path coverage.

records.title: Støfringsdal & Bolstad (2023), Optimizing (too) small ensemble rehearsal rooms for acoustic loud music
records.released_version: Proceedings of the Institute of Acoustics, vol. 45, part 2, Auditorium Acoustics 2023; DOI 10.25144/16014.
records.locator: Official Institute of Acoustics PDF, section 3.1 on the professional wind-band rehearsal room; direct-open tool error, relevant text surfaced in official-PDF search result.
records.observed_operation: Searched the exact title/DOI and reviewed the official proceedings PDF extract; direct open returned an internal error.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The case is a 1,600 m3 Norwegian professional wind-band room; previous work included 40 mm porous ceiling/wall absorbers. Musician survey reports a too-dry, imbalanced room and difficult mutual listening; several report overplaying.
records.applicability: A real internal-acoustics implementation history/tradeoff, not evidence for exterior isolation; scale and ensemble differ.

records.title: Shearer et al. (2021), Flexible control of acoustic conditions in a music rehearsal space using airbeds
records.released_version: Applied Acoustics, vol. 173, article 107708, published February 2021; DOI 10.1016/j.apacoust.2020.107708.
records.locator: London South Bank University author research record and abstract.
records.observed_operation: Opened the authors' university research record and read the abstract and bibliographic details.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Lab tests selected an inflated consumer airbed and room measurements compared Henry Wood Hall before/after installation; intended outcome was lower-band reverberation for flexible smaller-ensemble/voice use.
records.applicability: A reversible room-decay precedent only; not a sound-isolation or courtyard-disturbance result.
